reason: The sources provide at least 10 claims supported by at least two distinct sites describing Voyager 1's entry into interstellar space and its detection of the plasma hum.
story: Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 completed flybys of Jupiter, Saturn, and Titan before soaring toward the edge of our solar system. On August 25, 2012, it became the first human-made object to cross the heliopause and enter interstellar space. Because its primary plasma sensor failed back in 1980, scientists had to wait for solar outbursts to measure the surrounding interstellar medium. A massive solar eruption in 2012 finally reached the probe in 2013, vibrating the interstellar plasma around it like a violin string and revealing plasma tens of times denser than inside the solar bubble. Beyond these rare solar shocks, Voyager 1 detected a persistent, faint low-frequency hum vibrating through the cosmic gas—the eerie, continuous soundtrack of interstellar space itself. Powered by nuclear generators, Voyager 1 continues transmitting data across light-days of space, braving the deep vacuum alone.
angle: Deep in interstellar space, Voyager 1 detected an eerie, continuous low-frequency hum vibrating through interstellar plasma.

claims.claim: Voyager 1 launched 16 days after its twin craft, Voyager 2.
Voyager 1 conducted scientific flybys of Jupiter and Saturn.
Voyager 1 executed a close flyby of Saturn's largest moon, Titan.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space on August 25, 2012.
Voyager 1 was the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.
Voyager 1's direct plasma spectrometer stopped functioning in 1980.
A solar eruption from March 2012 triggered plasma oscillations at Voyager 1 in April 2013.
Interstellar plasma around Voyager 1 was measured to be significantly denser than plasma inside the solar bubble.
Voyager 1 detected a persistent, faint low-frequency hum vibrating in interstellar plasma.
Voyager 1 communicates with Earth using NASA's Deep Space Network.
Voyager 1 is powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by plutonium.
Mission engineers implemented a power management operation called the 'Big Bang' to extend Voyager 1's lifespan.
Engineers turned off Voyager 1's Low-Energy Charged Particles experiment in early 2026 to conserve electrical power.
Voyager 1 crossed the milestone distance of one light-day from Earth in November 2026.
Voyager 1 is traveling outbound in the direction of the constellation Ophiuchus.

disputed: The exact timing of when Voyager 1 crossed the termination shock is disputed between early 2003 and late 2004; scripts should attribute or omit specific dates.
The exact magnitude of plasma density increase upon entering interstellar space varies between sources (40-fold vs 80-fold); scripts should attribute as 'according to NASA observations'.
